canvas.title: Open20 Battle Maps

toast.mapRepaired: The map was damaged and has been repaired
toast.mapRepairedBody: An earlier save left extra data at the end of the file. The last saved version was opened and the file has been fixed.
toast.mapRepairedPending: An earlier save left extra data at the end of the file. The last saved version was opened; save the map to fix the file.
toast.missingPacks: {{count}} pack(s) used by this map aren't installed
toast.importedDungeondraft: Dungeondraft map imported. Saving creates a new .otbm file (the original is left untouched).
toast.fontsNotDownloaded_one: Couldn't download {{count}} font: those labels use the default one
toast.fontsNotDownloaded_other: Couldn't download {{count}} fonts: those labels use the default one
toast.backupRestoredBody: Save the map to keep it: until then, the file stays as it was.

prefs.title: Preferences
prefs.snapshotGestures: Move a snapshot while panning or zooming
prefs.snapshotGesturesHint: Smoother on slow devices and phones: the map looks blurry until you let go.

perf.measureHint: Draws the current map view several times, switching each part off in turn, and shows how much each adds to every frame. Open a map and leave the view as you use it.
perf.noMap: There's no open map to measure.
perf.frame: Still frame: {{ms}} ms (~{{fps}} frames per second)
perf.moveFrame: Frame while the view moves: {{ms}} ms (~{{fps}} frames per second)
perf.maxResolutionHint: Your screen: {{screen}}×. It weighs the most.
perf.maskDetail: Detail of caves, water, materials and lights

auto.title: Which one?
auto.hint: Tries each quality on a sample map (yours is left alone) and suggests the one running at ~60 frames per second.

graphicsIntro.title: Graphics on {{level}} quality
graphicsIntro.body: The app starts with graphics on {{level}} quality. You can tune it by hand in Preferences › Performance, or let it test this device and pick the best.
graphicsIntro.applied: Done: graphics on {{level}} (~{{fps}} frames per second). You can change it any time in Preferences › Performance.

debug.statsPanelHint: Shows frames per second and other drawing metrics over the map. The map only redraws when something changes: still, it reads 0 frames per second.
debug.graphicsDetailHint: Shows in Preferences › Performance the measurement of what each part of drawing costs (ms per frame).

storage.intro: What the app keeps on this device and how much space it takes. Only what the app makes or downloads again by itself can be cleared; packs are uninstalled.
storage.packsHint: {{count}} pack(s) installed. Uninstalling one removes it from the Library.
storage.thumbnailsHint: Asset previews. Cleared, they're made again while browsing the Library.
storage.fontsHint: {{count}} Google Fonts file(s). Cleared, they're downloaded again when a map uses them.
storage.otherHint: The pack registry and other files the app needs.

thumbnails.title: Clear thumbnails
thumbnails.confirm: Clear the Library's thumbnails? They're made again while browsing it, which can take a moment the first time.

fonts.title: Clear downloaded fonts
fonts.confirm: Clear the downloaded fonts? Maps that use them will ask to download them again.

about.title: About Open20 Battle Maps
about.desc: Open-source battle map editor for tabletop RPGs.
about.suite: An app of the Open20 suite

assets.title: Assets
assets.deleteConfirm: Delete {{count}} pack(s)? Files will be removed from disk.
assets.deactivateUsedConfirm: {{count}} of the selected pack(s) are used by the current map. Deactivating will delete the configurations that depend on them. This can't be undone — save your map first if you want to keep them.
assets.deleteUsedConfirm: {{count}} of the selected pack(s) are used by the current map. Deleting will remove the files from disk and delete the configurations that depend on them. This can't be undone — save your map first if you want to keep them.

tools.noPrefabs: No prefabs yet. Select items with the Select tool and save them.

tools.alphaPickHint: Clicking a transparent part of an object or portal selects what's under it, and a selection rectangle only picks them if it covers some of their visible part. When off, they're picked by their whole box.

library.noTags: The enabled packs have no tags for this category.

shortcuts.title: Keyboard shortcuts
shortcuts.fixedNote: Fixed: Ctrl+C / Ctrl+X / Ctrl+V, Ctrl+A, Esc, Enter, quick layers (1, 2, 3, 4, 7, 9, Alt+1, Alt+4), Ctrl+wheel and each tool's mouse gestures.

fonts.missingBody_one: The map's labels use {{count}} Google Fonts font that isn't downloaded: {{fonts}}. Download it? Otherwise they show in the default font.
fonts.missingBody_other: The map's labels use {{count}} Google Fonts fonts that aren't downloaded: {{fonts}}. Download them? Otherwise they show in the default font.

replaceAssets.title: Missing assets
replaceAssets.hint: Pick one to see it on the map and replace it with an asset from your packs. You can also click what's marked on the map.
replaceAssets.noneHint: Everything this map uses is available in your installed packs.
replaceAssets.suggestion: The closest match by name is suggested; search for another if it doesn't fit.

userPacks.createIntro: A pack keeps your images as objects, floors, walls and more. Edit it whenever you like and export it for Dungeondraft. Third-party packs (the ones you install from a file) can't be edited.
userPacks.firstPackHint: You haven't created any pack yet: one will be created with this name.
userPacks.author: Author
userPacks.removeChecked: Remove the selected ones from the list
userPacks.unreadableHint: This image couldn't be read ({{error}}). It won't be imported.
userPacks.noImages: No images. Add some with the ＋ button.
userPacks.pickToEdit: Pick one or more images from the list to adjust them.
userPacks.bulkEditing_other: Editing {{count}} items at once: changes apply to all.
userPacks.name: Name
userPacks.mixedTags: They have different tags: the ones you set replace them all.
userPacks.colorableHint: The image's red areas take the color you pick in the tool.
userPacks.skipUnreadable_one: {{count}} image can't be read and will be skipped
userPacks.skipUnreadable_other: {{count}} images can't be read and will be skipped
userPacks.readOnly: Third-party pack: it can't be edited. To add your images, create a new pack.
userPacks.exportedHint: Copy it to Dungeondraft's packs folder to use it there.
userPacks.selectHint: Tap an item to edit it; Ctrl/Shift or tap several to edit them together.
userPacks.nothingSelected: Pick an item to see and change its properties.
userPacks.nothingSelectedHint: You can select several and change them together.
userPacks.deleteAssetsConfirm_one: Delete this item from the pack?
userPacks.deleteUsedConfirm_one: This item is used in the open map: it will show as missing. Delete it anyway?
userPacks.deleteUsedConfirm_other: Some of these {{count}} items are used in the open map: they will show as missing. Delete them anyway?
userPacks.renameUsedTitle: Rename or move an item in use?
userPacks.renameUsedConfirm: The open map uses this item. Changing its name or folder makes the map show it as missing (you can replace it with the missing-assets tool). Continue?

categoryHint.portals: Doors and windows: they sit on walls; their width is what they take on the wall.
categoryHint.paths: A strip repeated along the path (its height is the path's width).
categoryHint.lights: A blob of light, usually white on transparent.
categoryHint.terrain: A texture repeated both ways; transparency sets how it blends.
categoryHint.tilesets: A floor texture repeated both ways.
categoryHint.walls: A horizontal strip repeated along the wall (its height is the thickness).
categoryHint.materials: A repeating tile, with an optional border.
categoryHint.caves: The cave's floor, with its wall texture.
categoryHint.roofs: The tiles, with edge, hip and ridge.

partsHint.walls: Pick “stone.png” and “stone_end.png” together and they pair up on their own.
partsHint.materials: Pick “grass_tile.png” and “grass_border.png” together and they pair up on their own.
partsHint.caves: Pick “floor.png” and “wall.png” from the same folder and they pair up on their own.
partsHint.roofs: Pick “tiles”, “edge”, “hip” and “ridge” together and they pair up on their own.

userPacks.emptyCreateHint: Or <1>create a pack</1> with your images.
userPacks.emptyTypeHint: This pack has nothing of this type yet. Import images to add some.
userPacks.thirdParty: Third-party pack: it can't be edited

optimize.buttonHint: Makes the pack take up much less space.
optimize.alreadyDone: Already optimized. Run it again if you added images.
optimize.title: Optimize images
optimize.intro_one: Compresses this pack's images so it takes up much less space. On the map the difference is barely noticeable.
optimize.intro_other: Compresses the images of these {{count}} packs so they take up much less space. On the map the difference is barely noticeable.
optimize.irreversible_one: The original images are replaced by the compressed ones and no copy is kept. To keep them, save the pack's file first.
optimize.irreversible_other: The original images are replaced by the compressed ones and no copy is kept. To keep them, save the packs' files first.
optimize.timeHint: Big packs can take a few minutes. You can stop whenever you like: what's already optimized stays that way.
optimize.runningHint: Closing this window stops it; what's already optimized stays that way.
optimize.stopping: Stopping after the images in progress…
optimize.stopped: Stopped. What was already optimized is saved.
optimize.stoppedHint: You can continue later: images already optimized are skipped.
optimize.nothing: It was already optimized: there was no more space to save.

essentials.tagline: Over 2,000 free assets for your maps.
essentials.name: Open20 Essentials

backups.title: Backups
backups.recoveryBody: Battle Maps closed unexpectedly with unsaved changes. The most recent backup is already picked: restore it to pick up where you left off.
backups.empty: No backups yet. While you edit a map, a backup is kept every few minutes, and another each time you save it.
backups.deleteBody: Delete every backup of “{{name}}”? The map file itself is left alone.
